territorial_scope.description: Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act, so it covers distributions concerning candidates for Federal office and Federal election activity.

evidence.quote: a person, political committee, or other entity may not knowingly distribute materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media of a covered individual

summary.short: Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to bar knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media of federal candidates, or in federal election activity, to influence an election or solicit funds. Candidates may seek injunctions and damages. Exempts bona fide news and satire. No effective date is stated.
summary.long: Section 2(a) adds new section 325 to Title III of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971. It defines a covered individual as a candidate for Federal office, and defines deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media as AI or machine-learning output that merges, replaces or superimposes content, or generates inauthentic content, and that a reasonable person would find to show a fundamentally different appearance or speech, or a person who did not actually exhibit it. Subsection (b) prohibits a person, political committee or other entity from knowingly distributing such media of a covered individual, or in Federal election activity, with intent to influence an election or solicit funds. Subsection (c) exempts licensed broadcasters and streaming services carrying such media in bona fide news coverage with a clear acknowledgement of authenticity questions, regularly published periodicals that clearly state the media does not accurately represent the covered individual, and satire or parody. Subsection (d) gives covered individuals a civil action for injunctive or equitable relief, and for general or special damages and attorney's fees, with a clear and convincing evidence burden on the plaintiff. Subsection (b) of the Act makes a violation of section 325 defamation per se for defamation actions. Subsection (c) contains a severability clause. The bill creates no public enforcement body or government fine, and states no effective date.

notes: Text is the introduced bill as provided; no later version or text_version metadata is in the document. target_instrument_id is left empty because no registry IDs were supplied for the FECA, the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure or any defamation law. The Sec. 2(d) civil action provisions are not the subject of relations entries; they are for the Tier A obligations/enforcement sections. Internal note: the prohibition in new sec. 325(b) applies to materially deceptive media of a covered individual (a Federal candidate) or to media distributed in carrying out a Federal election activity; the two limbs are stated in the alternative in the text.

events.note: The text states no dates. It has no introduction, passage, signature or effective-date provision, and no application, phase-in, deadline, sunset or repeal date. Section 2(a) adds new FECA section 325 without any commencement clause, and the bill's legislative history is not part of the fetched document, so no introduced event is recorded.

thresholds.note: The text contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its numbers are statutory citations (52 U.S.C. 30101; section 301(20)(A)(iii); section 325), and the provisions use categorical terms such as 'covered individual' (a candidate for Federal office), not numeric limits. The 'clear and convincing evidence' standard in subsection (d)(3) is an evidentiary standard, not a numeric threshold.
